mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines over the past 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.5 percentage points from the previous month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp from prior month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signal a contraction in the housing sector, which reduces consumer wealth and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 50% of instances when both RSAFS and HOUST decline, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index base 2017=100), the economy is in a supply shock contraction, which increases uncertainty and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past 3 months signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS increases over the past 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3 percentage points from the previous month signals accelerating inflation, which prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3pp from prior month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and residential fixed investment (RSAFS) signal a broad-based slowdown in consumer and housing demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 50% of instances when both GDPC1 and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% year-over-year), the Federal Reserve is likely to maintain a restrictive monetary policy, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL yoy change > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
